title: I Wanted to See the World

pages.title: The First Journeys
captions: I grew up in a coastal village in Xianxiang, Ningbo.
As a child, I often stayed in my dad's truck and travelled with him on deliveries.
That was my first glimpse of the world beyond home.
alt: A cargo truck on a road through a coastal village in Ningbo.
A boy riding beside his father in the cab of a truck.
The boy looking out of the truck window at the road beyond.

pages.title: A World Beyond Home
captions: Visits to relatives at Chinese New Year were my chance to see city life.
My sister would take me out to play. Those are some of my warmest childhood memories.
I came to believe that studying hard was my way out.
A good university could open up more possibilities.
alt: A family visiting relatives during Chinese New Year.
An older sister playing with her younger brother.
The boy studying at a desk at home.
The boy looking up from a book toward the window.

pages.title: Running, Jumping, Playing
captions: In fourth grade, I represented Xianxiang and won the Yinzhou district high jump competition.
I also came fourth in the 800 metres.
I kept training. In junior high, I often won the school's 400- and 800-metre races.
I started basketball in third grade. By sixth grade, I could do a between-the-legs layup.
alt: A schoolboy clearing the bar in a high jump competition.
The boy running an 800-metre race.
A junior-high student crossing the finish line.
A boy performing a basketball layup.

pages.title: The Door I Almost Reached
captions: My grades were uneven in my first two years of junior high.
In my final year, I caught up.
I qualified for a top provincial high school's special admissions exam.
But I fell short of the minimum score.
alt: A junior-high student facing several school subjects.
The student revising with growing concentration.
The student looking hopeful about an admissions opportunity.
The student looking quietly disappointed by exam results.

pages.title: Back to the Desk
captions: That setback hit me hard. Its shadow stayed with me for years.
Under enormous pressure, I returned to preparing for the regular high school entrance exam.
In the end, I finished first in my class.
I entered Zhengshi High School in Ningbo, still some way from what I had hoped for.
alt: A student sitting alone after a disappointing exam.
The student returning to his entrance-exam revision.
The student holding his class results.
The student entering a high-school campus in Ningbo.

pages.title: Under Other People's Gaze
captions: As I grew through high school, my underbite became severe.
I was given hurtful nicknames and mocked.
I became painfully aware of how others saw me. My confidence faded.
Being around people gradually became stressful.
alt: A high-school student seeing his pronounced underbite in the mirror.
The student feeling self-conscious in a school corridor.
The student standing apart from a group.
The student walking alone toward his dormitory.

pages.title: A Light in the Night
captions: Some nights, I hid in the dormitory bathroom and cried.
I woke early, stayed up late, and poured much of my time into studying.
In my last two years of high school, I often ranked first in my year. English had always come naturally to me.
alt: A quiet dormitory corridor and a student at the bathroom doorway.
The student wiping away tears, with his pre-surgery jaw visible.
The student studying under a warm desk lamp at night.
The student concentrating on an English book.

pages.title: Learning and Teaching
captions: My university entrance exam did not go as well as I had hoped.
I chose Zhejiang Gongshang University over a Project 211 university outside Zhejiang.
I began teaching English after high school. I have kept teaching ever since.
I loved languages and trusted my ability to learn them, so I chose to major in French.
University gave me more freedom, but the distress over my jaw remained.
alt: A high-school graduate considering his university exam results.
The graduate weighing his university choices.
The young man beginning to teach English.
An undergraduate opening a French coursebook.
The undergraduate walking across campus before jaw surgery.

pages.title: My Family Beside Me
captions: My family took me to Shanghai Ninth People's Hospital for a consultation.
I decided to have corrective jaw surgery.
Before surgery, I needed orthodontic treatment.
It lasted more than two years, much longer than I had expected.
alt: A young man and his family in a hospital waiting area.
The family listening to a doctor during a consultation.
An orthodontic appointment before jaw surgery.
Calendar pages suggesting the long wait during treatment.

pages.title: After the Long Wait
captions: During treatment, my underbite became more pronounced, and the emotional strain grew.
I withdrew from social life and focused on studying. I consistently ranked first in my major, academically and overall.
In the second semester of my junior year, I finally had surgery.
alt: An undergraduate sitting alone during orthodontic treatment.
The undergraduate studying, his pre-surgery jaw clearly visible.
The young man with a family member before surgery.
The young man resting by a hospital window after surgery.

pages.title: A Brighter Chapter
captions: Surgery changed my appearance. I began to regain the confidence to face everyday life.
Two months later, I secured recommended admission to the School of International Business at Southwestern University of Finance and Economics.
I also received the National Scholarship. After so much pressure and waiting, it was a bright moment in my life.
alt: A university student walking on campus after jaw surgery.
The student receiving news of postgraduate admission.
The student standing in warm campus light with a folder.

pages.title: Into the Working World
captions: After securing my postgraduate place, I interned at Mingle Advisors, a Finnish firm in Hangzhou.
After graduation, I worked in French-speaking overseas sales at Market Union in Ningbo, helping close nearly US$1 million in orders.
Then I moved to Chengdu for graduate school.
Chengdu was a happy chapter. I studied, interned at Alliance Française, and continued teaching English.
alt: An internship in a small company office in Hangzhou.
Working in overseas sales in Ningbo.
Arriving in Chengdu for graduate study.
Studying and preparing language lessons in Chengdu.

pages.title: Choosing to Go
captions: Then came another choice: should I study abroad?
Going would mean delaying graduation.
I thought about it for a long time. Since childhood, I had wanted to see the world.
I chose a one-year exchange at Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne University.
alt: Reading about an overseas exchange programme.
Weighing the exchange against a later graduation.
A window scene echoing the childhood truck journeys.
Preparing exchange application papers and a travel bag.

pages.title: A New Direction
captions: Before leaving, I spent four months in overseas talent recruitment at ByteDance in Chengdu.
I helped ByteDance's Seed AI team recruit top talent in North America.
That experience drew me into AI and pushed me to learn more.
With a new direction taking shape, I left for Paris.
alt: An overseas recruitment internship in Chengdu.
Supporting a remote talent recruitment conversation.
Learning about AI through books and notes.
Looking out of an airplane window on the way to Paris.

pages.title: The Limits of My World
captions: During my year in Paris, I also spent a year learning Spanish.
I have always loved languages. I explored Paris, France, and other parts of Europe.
The limits of my language are the limits of my world.
pages.closingCaption: The child who wanted to see the world had finally made it.
alt: An exchange student taking notes in a Spanish-language class in Paris.
The student exploring a European street with a day bag.
The student walking along a sunlit Paris street.

pages.title: Still Exploring
captions: After returning from Paris, I joined Tencent Cloud as a direct sales intern.
My experience with AI helped me find my direction. I keep building with AI and learning more about cloud computing.
I have taught English since leaving high school. Years of experience have only deepened my enthusiasm for teaching.
Languages opened up my world. And there is still so much I want to explore.
alt: Starting work in cloud sales.
Building and learning with AI on a laptop.
Teaching English with confidence and enthusiasm.
Looking through a window, with books and a laptop nearby.
